items.excerpt: Dr. Dre says he is now “embracing” AI in the studio, calling it “a new tool for creativity” and arguing that only people “who have trouble creating” see it as a threat.
Dr. Dre compares AI resistance to earlier panics over drum machines and synths, and says plenty of producers are already using AI quietly without admitting it.
Hotone's pocket-sized Pulze Jr. modelling amp puts onboard AI tone-matching and assistive presets into a battery-powered practice amp for guitarists.

Ohlhorst Digital's Trama is a free offline stem separator for Windows, macOS and Linux that splits tracks into vocals, drums, bass and other using a fine-tuned Hybrid Transformer Demucs model — no uploads, no subscription.
A breakdown of Round Hill's billion-dollar suits against Suno and Anthropic: the publisher targets model weights and extraction tools, and says it wants a jury trial rather than a settlement.
SOS reviews SpectraLayers Pro 13, Steinberg's spectral editor whose AI-driven unmixing, dialogue and noise processing keep pushing what you can surgically repair or rebuild inside a mix.
Musical Spirograph is a free browser toy that turns doodled geometric loops into generative compositions — a low-stakes way to sketch algorithmic musical ideas.
Cyanite's Tagging 2.0 adds lyric analysis, tempo, vocal style, use-case and structural segmentation models plus a scalable API, reshaping how catalogues get searched and pitched.
Udio and Grai become the first licensees of the UMG-backed Music IP Holdings AI patent pool, a possible template for how licensed AI music tools get built.
Jimmy Iovine argues AI music companies have failed to explain themselves to artists, framing the standoff as a communication problem as much as a legal one.
With regulators requiring AI outputs to be machine-detectable, MIDiA asks whether watermarking actually slows AI content flooding streaming — or just relabels it.
A practical guide to getting artist and venue sites cited by AI assistants — structured data, canonical bios and the on-page work that decides what chatbots say about you.
MiniMax Music 3 lands as an open-weights text-to-music model that generates full five-minute songs locally, with ComfyUI and Diffusers workflows that run on a single 24GB GPU.
ARIA sets new eligibility rules that exclude fully or mostly AI-generated recordings from Australia's official charts, while allowing AI-assisted human work.
Yurt Rock's Dr. Fill is a drum-fill library built from real captured performances and marketed explicitly with “no AI in sight” — a sign of how sample makers now position craft against generation.
AI-powered creation suite Tamber hits 2.0 with a reworked interface and new generation and editing features aimed at producers who want AI inside a conventional workflow.
